drug_class: CCR5 antagonist (a type of antiretroviral medication used to treat HIV)
purpose: Maraviroc is used to treat HIV infection in adults and children. It is always used in combination with other HIV medications, never alone. It helps keep the amount of HIV in your body at a very low level so your immune system can stay stronger.
how_it_works: HIV needs to grab onto a specific doorway on your immune cells called the CCR5 receptor to get inside and infect them. Maraviroc works by blocking that doorway, so the virus cannot get in. Think of it like putting a lock on the door so HIV cannot enter your cells.
common_side_effects: Cough, fever, upper respiratory infections (like a cold), rash, dizziness, stomach pain, muscle and joint pain, and feeling tired. Some people may also notice changes in their sleep or mild nausea.
warnings: Maraviroc can rarely cause serious liver problems — tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain. It may also cause low blood pressure, especially when standing up quickly, which can make you feel dizzy or faint. Before starting this medicine, your doctor will do a special test to make sure this drug will work for your type of HIV. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 150 mg, 300 mg, or 600 mg taken by mouth twice a day, depending on the other HIV medications you are taking. Your doctor will determine the right dose for you. It can be taken with or without food. Try to take it at the same times each day to keep it working consistently.
